title: validation_store digests a component's current seals
intention: validation_store answers, in one string, the current seal state of a whole component, so a dependent can record it and later tell whether it moved.
traces_to: Law 9 via 1b6516f92db3 and parent 50e0581737e8 (yellow on a dependency's move needs a comparable token for 'the dependency's seals'). RULE 1: the store owns seals, so the digest is the store's.
how: (a) def seal_digest(component_dir: str) -> str in validation_store.py. (b) Iterate sorted(glob(<dir>/validations/*.json)). For each, records = read_validations(path=f), skip it when records is empty, and take cur = records[-1] if it is a list, else records. If cur is not a dict, raise ValueError(f). (c) Add the row [Path(f).stem, cur.get('verdict'), (cur.get('evidence') or {}).get('source_fingerprint')]. (d) Return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(rows, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest(). (e) Proof: cairn/tools/validation_store/proofs/test_seal_digest.py, fixture validations files in a tempdir, PROVES keyed on this ticket, clauses 1-5, one tooth each.
falsifier: Done when cairn/tools/validation_store/proofs/test_seal_digest.py is green under bin/cairn test --netns. (1) Two calls over an unchanged fixture component return the same 64-hex string. (2) Changing a current record's evidence.source_fingerprint changes the digest. (3) Changing its verdict changes the digest. (4) Appending an older entry before the last, or changing only a timestamp field, leaves the digest unchanged. (5) A component with no validations dir returns the sha256 of the canonical empty list. Red at HEAD 4b3ac7f5: no seal_digest.
